cards.back: A branch of AI where systems **learn from data without explicit programming**. Types: **Supervised** (labeled), **Unsupervised** (patterns in unlabeled), **Reinforcement** (trial & error, rewards).
**AI4SE** = AI tools improving SE tasks (Copilot, test automation). **SE4AI** = applying SE principles to build reliable AI systems (scalability, safety, maintainability).
**ML is data-driven** (probabilistic, experimental, evaluated by accuracy/precision/recall). **SE is process-driven** (deterministic code, structured, evaluated by functional correctness).

**SDLC still governs** the process · **human oversight is non-negotiable** (validate every AI suggestion) · **new skills, not new fundamentals**. Risks: incorrect/insecure code, over-reliance, reduced critical thinking.

**Model** = mathematical construct that predicts. **System** = the whole ecosystem (data, deployment, monitoring, scaling). e.g. a CNN vs the entire Apollo self-driving system (many models + non-ML code).
Model Requirements → Data Collection & Cleaning → Data Labeling → Feature Engineering → Model Training & Tuning → Model Evaluation → Deployment & Monitoring.
**DevOps** versions **code**, deploys software. **MLOps** also versions **data & models** and adds **continuous training/validation/retraining**. Apps: fraud detection, healthcare, recommendations.

ML errors are **expected**. Use fault-tolerant design, human-in-the-loop, undoable actions, monitoring, **guardrails** (block prompt injection, PII exposure). Safety often comes from **outside** the model (Smart Toaster: code check + thermal fuse).
**Input** = the design document. **Output** = executable software (input to testing). Tool-intensive, knowledge-intensive, quality-focused, high-volume output.
**PascalCase** for classes, **camelCase** for methods; identifiers **2–3 to 30 chars**; avoid keyword-like names; comments explain the **"why," not the "what."**
An ambiguity where an `else` could pair with **more than one preceding `if`**. The compiler pairs it with the **nearest** `if` — use braces to disambiguate.

**Standards** = mandatory rules; **Guidelines** = recommendations. **Defensive programming** follows **Murphy's Law** ("if anything can go wrong, it will") — anticipate/handle errors, check assumptions.
**① Validate input ② Heed compiler warnings ③ Default Deny ④ Least Privilege ⑤ Sanitize data** sent to other systems (prevents injection).

cards.front: Testable programming: stub vs harness vs scaffolding
cards.back: **Stub** = replaces a *called* lower-level module (fixed values, top-down). **Test Harness** = stubs + drivers + data to automate execution. **Scaffolding** = throwaway code that supports a test.
Inspections detect **55–60%** of defects (vs unit **25%**, integration **45%**). AT&T: **+14% productivity, −90% defects**. Industry: Google, Yelp ('Ship It!'), Facebook.

**Static** = no execution, reasons about all paths, may have **false positives** (linters, SonarQube). **Dynamic** = executes, findings real but limited to test inputs (**false negatives**). Best QA **combines** both.
$327M lost to an **undetected unit mismatch** (pound-force vs newton) — the kind of bug **type checking / static analysis** catches.
**Commit → Build → Unit Tests → Integration Tests → Staging → Acceptance → Production.** CI builds/tests on commits; CD deploys validated changes. Keep a deployable state, minimise errors.

Three roles: define tasks/resources, define dependencies (**graph**), execute tasks. Uses a **Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)** so a task runs only after its dependencies — enabling correct, incremental builds.
Merge to main **frequently** (daily); auto build/test each merge. **Pro:** find integration problems early; mainline always works. **Con:** large systems are slow to build/test; platform differences.
**Dev + Ops** combined for high-velocity delivery; extends Agile (Amazon deploys every **11.7s**). Pillars: **Collaboration, Affinity, Tools, Scaling**.
Continuous **Integration → Build → Testing → Delivery → Deployment**. *Delivery* = always deployable, release on demand. *Deployment* = auto-ship every validated change to prod (no manual gate).
Automates **security at every SDLC phase** as a shared responsibility — *"software, safer, sooner."* **Shift left** = move security testing toward developers (find/fix flaws as code is written).

*"Testing shows the presence of bugs, never their absence."* The 7: presence-not-absence, exhaustive-impossible, **start early**, defect clustering, **pesticide paradox**, context-dependent, **V ≠ V**.

**Verify** = "building the product **right**?" (vs specs). **Validate** = "building the **right** product?" (vs user needs). Static testing = verification; dynamic testing = validation. (V&V = "Very Very Important.")
**Black-box** = tests from the **spec** (no code view) — EP, BVA, pairwise; no implementation bias. **White-box** = tests from **code paths** — line/branch coverage.
Divide inputs into **classes treated the same**; test **one per class**. *"If one works, all work; if one fails, all fail."* e.g. Age 18–65 → classes <18, 18–65, >65.
Errors cluster at **edges**. For range [min,max] test **min−1, min, max, max+1**. e.g. password length 8–15 → test **7, 8, 15, 16**.
Cover every **pair** of parameter values with a minimal test set → catches **50–90%** of defects. Misses 3-way+ interactions and parameter dependencies.

**Positive** (does what it should — valid login → access), **Negative** (rejects what it shouldn't — invalid email → error), **Destructive** (how much before breaking — 1000 logins/sec). Every test needs an **Expected Result**.
Reliability = probability of **failure-free operation** for a time in an environment. **Predictive** models → **MTTF**; **Assessment** models → **MTBF**, failure rate, fault density.
**V(G) = E − N + 2P** (= decisions + 1) from the Control Flow Graph. = independent paths = min test cases for path coverage. Bands: 1–10 low, 11–20 moderate, 21–50 high, **>50 redesign**.
**Inspections** = static (no execution; reviews/walkthroughs/Fagan) — errors don't mask, incomplete code OK, **60–90%** detection. **Testing** = dynamic (run with data).

**Unit** (functions/classes in isolation — defect testing) → **Component** (composite, test the interface) → **System** (integration & emergent properties). Inheritance complicates object-class testing.

**Interface misuse** (wrong param order), **interface misunderstanding** (wrong assumptions), **timing errors** (out-of-date data). Guidelines: extreme params, **always test null pointers**, design tests to fail.

**Alpha** = friendly users **with the dev team at the developer's site**. **Beta** = external users in the real environment, pre-release. **Acceptance** = customer's **go/no-go** in their environment.
**Regression** = re-run **all** tests after a change (must pass before commit; automate). **Release** = a separate team validates a release is good enough for external use (black-box, **Go/No-Go**).
**Profiling** = measure performance to find **CPU/memory bottlenecks** (VisualVM, cProfile). **Tracing** = track **execution flow / call sequence** (deadlocks). Fail CI build if **>5% slower**.
Run under significant load for **8–72 hours at 70–80%** load to find **memory leaks, connection leaks, thread-pool exhaustion** — the slow killers short tests miss.

**Break things on purpose in production** (minimized blast radius) to build resilience. **Netflix Chaos Monkey** kills instances; SPS stays flat → 99.99% availability. Tools: Chaos Monkey, Chaos Mesh, Gremlin.
Both inject faults. **Fault seeding** calibrates the **test process** (what % of seeded faults do testers find?). **Mutation testing** evaluates the **test suite** (do tests kill all mutants?).

Discipline to **control & track changes** to artifacts (CIs); provides **reproducible builds, audit trails/traceability, concurrent work, controlled change**. Tracks who/why/when via versioning/branching/merging.
**Configuration Manager** (policies, baselining), **Developer**, **Build/Release Engineer**, **QA**, **Change Control Board (CCB)** (approve high-risk changes), **Auditor**.

**CI** = anything needed to **reproduce the product** (source, scripts, manifests, test data, IaC). Directories: **Programmer** (working copy), **Repository** (artifacts), **Master** (controlled baselines).
An agreed, **frozen snapshot** of CIs; changed only via formal change control. Types: **Functional** (design), **Development** (integration snapshot), **Release** (final tested version).

**Trunk-based** (main + short branches, promotes CI), **Gitflow** (feature/release/hotfix), **release-per-customer**. **Hotfix:** branch from release tag, merge to release **and** main. Versioning: **MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH**.
**CR → validity check → impact & cost analysis → CCB selects → implement → test → verify & close.** Overseen by the **CCB**; tracked via a change-request form + derivation history.
① consequences of **not** changing ② benefits ③ number of users affected ④ cost (dev/test/docs/training) ⑤ fit with the release cycle.
**New → (Rejected/Duplicate/Deferred)/Assigned → In Progress → Fixed → Closed** (or **Reopened**). Track **MTTR** & reopen rate; link fixes to commits. (Word 'teh'→'the' = improvement, not bug.)

**Source control** (RCS, CVS, ClearCase, GitHub), **build**, **install**, **bug tracking** (Bugzilla, Jira). **Make** = general, explicit Makefile rules; **Maven** = Java, convention-over-config (`pom.xml`).
Centralised log/track/manage with audit trails: **Bugzilla, FogBugz, Trac, Redmine, Jira, Backlog**. GitHub flow: **fork → change → pull request → merge**.

Machine-readable **inventory of all components** (name, version, license, checksum). Instantly answers "are we affected?" for CVEs like **Log4Shell**. Standards: **SPDX, CycloneDX, SWID**; tools: Syft, Trivy.
